content:
Although this week's iOS 27 public beta has stolen the spotlight, Apple has also released a new public beta firmware for AirPods at the same time. This update finally brings a long-awaited feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods public beta details

The AirPods public beta firmware version is 9.0.314, with build number 9A314b. The following AirPods models can be updated:

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C versions)
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation
  • AirPods Max 2

You can opt into the AirPods public beta through the Settings app on your iPhone. When your AirPods are connected, a toggle will appear in the Settings app, allowing you to enable the beta firmware. After that, as long as your AirPods are in their charging case and within range of your paired iPhone, the beta will be automatically downloaded and installed.

  • Open the Settings app
  • Tap "Bluetooth"
  • Tap the (i) icon next to your AirPods
  • Scroll down and enable "AirPods Beta Updates"

Custom EQ officially lands on AirPods

After installing the AirPods public beta, you'll find a long-awaited new feature in the Settings app: custom EQ.

Thanks to the new custom EQ controls, you can now fine-tune your AirPods' sound more precisely. In the Settings app, you can adjust the bass, mids, and treble of your AirPods.

Apple explains: "AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully reproduce the original sound of music, TV shows, movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound style, you can customize how your AirPods sound when playing any audio."

While adjusting the custom EQ, you can play songs from Apple Music directly within the Settings app to hear the effect of your adjustments in real time.

This is by no means the most advanced equaliser feature currently available—it's just a basic three-band system. But regardless, this is an AirPods feature users have waited a long time for, and Apple has finally given users the ability to customise—even though most people will probably stick with the default settings.

You can find the new custom EQ feature in the "Audio & Routing" menu of the AirPods section in the Settings app. All AirPods equipped with the H2 chip support this feature, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods

Below are other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods:

  • Redesigned Settings app: iOS 27 redesigns the AirPods interface within the Settings app. Controls have been reorganised, with separate dedicated menus for Hearing Health, Find My, Live Translation, and more.
  • Adaptive Audio slider: A new slider has been added in the Settings app, allowing you to fine-tune the Adaptive Audio mode more precisely.
  • GymKit: Although GymKit has been around for several years, it has always required pairing with an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac noted, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to the iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
  • Precision Finding: You can now use the Precision Finding feature in the Find My app on your Apple Watch to locate your AirPods Pro 3.
  • Siri AI: AirPods can interact with Siri AI when paired with a compatible iPhone.

Wrapping up

Which new AirPods feature are you most looking forward to trying? Will you give the new custom EQ a go? Let us know in the comments section below.
